subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose anonymous Talk activity to plugins

question: Should OpenClaw publish a Plugin SDK API that lets any loaded plugin observe anonymous timing and state for every Talk session in the process, or must Talk activity be limited by a declared capability and owner/session scope?
rationale: Payload redaction protects content but does not settle whether cross-plugin behavioral metadata is an allowed SDK disclosure; that trust boundary is a product and security contract requiring maintainer intent.

options.title: Require scoped observation
options.body: Expose activity only to a plugin with an explicit reviewed capability and bind events to the session or route it owns.

options.title: Approve global observation
options.body: Document that all loaded plugins may observe anonymous process-wide Talk activity and accept this as a permanent Plugin SDK privacy contract.

options.title: Defer the SDK surface
options.body: Keep the activity recorder internal until a supported plugin trust model and consumer need are approved.

recommendation.title: Require scoped observation
recommendation.body: Expose activity only to a plugin with an explicit reviewed capability and bind events to the session or route it owns.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the recent merged Talk-session refactor and the proposed SDK surface, so they are the closest technical owner for clarifying the intended scope.
